channel.title: Nature Computational Science
channel.description:
Nature Computational Science is a multidisciplinary journal that focuses on the development and use of computational techniques and mathematical models, as well as their application to address complex problems across a range of scientific disciplines. The journal publishes both fundamental and applied research, from groundbreaking algorithms, tools and frameworks that notably help to advance scientific research, to methodologies that use computing capabilities in novel ways to find new insights and solve challenging real-world problems. By doing so, the journal creates a unique environment to bring together different disciplines to discuss the latest advances in computational science.   Disciplines covered by Nature Computational Science include, but are not limited to:
  • Bioinformatics
  • Cheminformatics
  • Geoinformatics
  • Climate Modeling and Simulation
  • Computational Physics and Cosmology
  • Applied Math
  • Materials Science
  • Urban Science and Technology
  • Scientific Computing
  • Methods, Tools and Platforms for Computational Science
  • Visualization and Virtual Reality for Computational Science
Nature Computational Science is committed to publishing significant, high-quality research through a fair and rigorous peer-review process that is overseen by a team of full-time professional editors.

item.title: Making the case for a non-primary article
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01078-7

Author-proposed non-primary articles can bring fresh and timely perspectives to the journal. Here, we discuss the factors that editors consider when assessing proposals for these contributions.

item.content:encoded:

Structure coefficients provide a unified way to identify dynamic network structures that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

item.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9

The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

item.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01067-w

An automated framework, HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), is developed that integrates ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly for the structure prediction of large protein complexes. Across three benchmarks, HDM demonstrates increased accuracy and robustness in modeling large protein assemblies, compared with state-of-the-art assembly and deep learning-based methods.
item.dc:title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
item.dc:source: Nature Computational Science, Published online: 2026-10-15; | doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01067-w
